headline: FedEx grows revenue but profit slips as spin-off closes
summary_short: Fourth-quarter revenue rose 13% year-over-year to $25.0 billion, but GAAP operating income fell 13% to $1.55 billion as FedEx absorbed $298 million of FedEx Freight spin-off costs; diluted EPS was $6.60, down 4% from $6.88 a year ago.
summary_long: GAAP results were pressured by $298M of FedEx Freight spin-off costs, $204M of business-optimization charges, and a $150M retirement-plan mark-to-market adjustment; adjusted (non-GAAP) operating income rose to $2.09 billion (+3% y/y) on higher U.S. Domestic and International Priority yields, transformation cost savings, and higher export volume, partly offset by higher purchased-transportation and wage costs. The FedEx Freight spin-off completed June 1, 2026, distributing 80.1% of Freight's shares to FedEx holders; FedEx retains 19.9% for disposal within 24 months. Cash rose to $13.3 billion, lifted by a $4.1 billion spin-off dividend. FedEx introduced CY2026 guidance: revenue growth of ~11%, adjusted diluted EPS of $16.90-$18.10 from continuing operations.
